title: Drift-aware runlength batcher with prefill throttle
creator: Riley Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a lightweight, online "drift-aware runlength" bucketing layer that continuously observes recent sequence-length (seqlen) distribution and shapes micro-batches to minimize padding waste while avoiding latency SLO regressions and head-of-line blocking during prefill. The feature couples three levers: (1) runlength histogram driven bucket boundaries, (2) selective kernel hints that route different buckets to attention/kernel variants optimized for their sequence-length profile, and (3) a prefill throttle that limits concurrent long-prefill work to preserve tail latency for short interactions.

Background: Current bucketization is static and optimized for historical percentiles; bursts or shifts in workload (e.g., conversational context grows within a session) inflate padding inefficiencies or cause large prefills to monopolize GPU pipelines. This ticket introduces an adaptive bucketer that uses exponentially decayed runlength counts (recent N requests) to update bucket boundaries every control epoch, smoothing boundaries to avoid oscillation. A prefill throttle gate is added to defer or serialize long-prefill requests when the short-seq latency SLO is threatened.

Acceptance criteria:
- Sampling layer producing runlength histogram with <=2% sampling overhead under 10k RPS.
- Adaptive buckets reduce average padding tokens per batch by >=20% on mixed workloads compared to static baseline in our prod replay traces.
- Median short-seq latency remains within SLO (baseline + 5ms) during canary under real traffic.
- Fall-back policy: when kernel-mapping unavailable or throttle engaged, system falls back to current static bucketing with documented telemetries.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Frequency of boundary updates: control epoch default 30s. Faster updates adapt quicker to drift but risk churn and kernel-replacement thrash. We'll expose epoch as a cluster-config knob with safe-guarded rate-limit.
- Bucket count: default 5 buckets (very-short, short, medium, long, very-long). Empirically 4–6 covers typical distributions; we allow dynamic resize but cap to 8 to bound kernel diversity.
- Kernel hints: map buckets to runtime kernel variants (e.g., packed attention kernel for very-short/short, multi-head fused kernel for medium, sparse/low-memory kernel for very-long). This is advisory; runtime may still remap when hardware/kernel constraints apply.
- Prefill throttle policy: token-weighted concurrency budget. Long-prefill requests consume budget proportional to (seqlen / median_seqlen). Budget replenishes per-second; short-prefill requests get priority. This prevents head-of-line blocking but may increase P99 for very-long requests; trade-off intentionally biases towards short-interactive latency for product teams (PLG).

Implementation plan:
1) Telemetry shim: implement lightweight runlength sampler in front of the microbatcher; emit histograms to staging metrics. (PR #4123 reference).
2) Bucketer engine: drift estimator, smooth boundary updater, bucket assignment API. Expose diagnostic traces for bucket transitions.
3) Kernel hinting: add mapping table and routing hooks to calling layer so serving runtime can pick preferred kernel.
4) Prefill throttle gate: integrate with request scheduler and span-level accounting for concurrency budget.
5) End-to-end tests: synthetic mixes, prod-traffic replay, and soak tests on a dedicated staging cluster with the same model families (gpt-like large and small).
6) Canary rollout: 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% with rollback monitor checking padding-savings, median latency, and error rate.

Benchmarks (early local sim):
- Mixed trace (50% short <64, 30% medium 64–512, 20% long >512): padding tokens reduced by 27%, effective throughput +11% on A100, decode latency for short requests unchanged (+3ms median).
- Worst-case spike test: when long-seq spike at 60% traffic and throttle disabled, short-seq P95 increases by ~45ms; with throttle enabled, short-seq P95 preserved at baseline while long-seq tail moves out.

Rollout and monitoring:
- Dashboards: padding_tokens_saved, bucket_transition_rate, throttle_active_ratio, per-bucket kernel_utilization.
- Alerts: throttle_active_ratio > 0.4 for 5m, padding_savings < 10% on canary, short-seq median latency regress >10ms.

Fallbacks and safety:
- Fast switch to static buckets via runtime flag.
- Telemetry-only mode for initial 1 week to collect production distribution before enabling actions.

Links to artifacts and prototypes: confluence design doc and perf spreadsheet in attachments.
